title: Conditional Machine Simulation
statement: Let $D,M_1,M_2$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, and let $p$ map Boolean words to truth values. Suppose $D$ computes the one-symbol word $[p(x)]$ on every input $x$, halting after some finite number of steps. Then there is a finite Boolean Turing machine $M$ such that, for every pair of Boolean words $x,w$, $M$ halts on input $x$ with output $w$ after some finite number of steps if and only if the machine selected by $p(x)$—namely $M_1$ when $p(x)$ is true and $M_2$ otherwise—halts on $x$ with output $w$ after some finite number of steps.
hypotheses_covered: $D$ computes $[p(x)]$ on every input $x$ after some finite number of steps
replaced:
Let $D$, $M_1$, $M_2$ be multi-tape Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet
and let $p$ be a Boolean-valued predicate on Boolean words such that $D$
computes the function $x \mapsto [p(x)]$: on every input $x$ it eventually
halts with the single symbol $p(x)$ as its output.  Then there exists a
machine $M$ such that for all Boolean words $x$ and $w$: $M$ halts on input
$x$ with output $w$ (within some number of steps) if and only if the branch
machine selected by $p(x)$ — namely $M_1$ when $p(x)$ is true and $M_2$ when
$p(x)$ is false — halts on that same input $x$ with output $w$ (within some
number of steps).
